record.original_question: Give a proof, without relying on a lengthy computer search, that every Type II [48, 24, 12] code is equivalent to q48, and determine whether q48 is in fact the unique [48, 24, 12] code even without the Type II restriction.

evidence.quote: Open Question 9.1. Prove without a lengthy computer search that a Type II [48, 24, 12] code is unique (i.e., equivalent to the q48). Prove or disprove that q48 is a unique [48, 24, 12] code.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A binary linear code of length $n$ and dimension $k$ is a $k$-dimensional subspace $C \subseteq \mathbb{F}_2^n$. Its minimum distance $d$ is the smallest Hamming weight of a nonzero codeword. The code is self-dual if $C = C^\perp$ under the standard inner product, and it is Type II (doubly even) if it is self-dual and every codeword has weight divisible by $4$. A $[48,24,12]$ code is a binary linear code with the indicated parameters. Two codes are equivalent if one is obtained from the other by a permutation of coordinates. Let $q_{48}$ denote the extended binary quadratic residue code of length $48$, which is a Type II $[48,24,12]$ code.

(a) Give a proof, not relying on a lengthy computer search, that every Type II $[48,24,12]$ binary linear code is equivalent to $q_{48}$.

(b) Determine whether $q_{48}$ is the unique (up to equivalence) binary linear $[48,24,12]$ code, without imposing the Type II restriction; that is, prove or disprove that every binary $[48,24,12]$ code is equivalent to $q_{48}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The Type II uniqueness of the [48,24,12] code (equivalence to the extended quadratic residue code q48) was established by Houghten, Lam, Thiel and Parker via a computer search, so part (a)—a proof without a lengthy computer search—appears to remain open. The general uniqueness question (without the Type II restriction) does not appear to have been resolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: The extended quadratic residue code is the only (48,24,12) self-dual doubly-even code
status_evidence.snippet: The search for a (48,24,12) self-dual doubly-even code can be partitioned into three cases... establishing that the extended quadratic residue code is the only doubly-even self-dual (48,24,12) code.
status_evidence.claim: Type II uniqueness was proved via computer search, not by a conceptual proof.

status_evidence.title: A Characterization of Designs Related to an Extremal Doubly-Even Self-Dual Code of Length 48
status_evidence.snippet: The uniqueness of a binary doubly-even self-dual [48,24,12] code is used to prove uniqueness of related designs.
status_evidence.claim: Type II uniqueness is established and used in further work; non-Type-II uniqueness not addressed.
